name: Kingdomino
edition: Base game, Blue Orange multilingual rules (English section); print year not stated in the text

setup.text: Shuffle the dominoes and stack them as a draw pile with the numbered sides facing out.
Draw dominoes equal to the kings in play and line them up by number, lowest next to the box, then flip them to show the terrain.
Take a starting tile and the castle in your colour. Put the castle on the tile, in front of you.
Take the kings of your colour.

by_count.2: Take both kings of your colour.

setup.text: One player holds all the kings, and players draw one at random in turn, placing it on a domino of their choice. One king per domino.
Then draw a new line from the pile, ordered by number, and flip it. In a 2-player game each player picks 2 dominoes, one for each king.

turn.summary: Players act in the order their kings sit on the first line, lowest number first. Each does two actions.
steps: Add the domino your king is on to your kingdom, following the connection rules.
Move your king to a domino in the new line.
When everyone has acted, form a new line and start the next turn.
In a 2-player game, each player does both actions twice per turn, once per king.
Connection rule: join it to your starting tile, which matches any terrain, or match at least 1 terrain of another domino, horizontally or vertically.
If a domino cannot be placed legally or fit in your 5x5 grid, discard it.

end: After the last dominoes are lined up, everyone takes one final turn. Each player should then have a kingdom in a 5x5 grid, though it may be incomplete after discards.

scoring.text: A territory is a group of squares of the same terrain joined horizontally or vertically.
Multiply the squares in a territory by the crowns in it. A territory with no crowns scores 0.
Add up the scores of all your territories. Highest total wins.

tiebreak: Largest single territory wins; then most crowns; if still tied, share the win.

missed.text: Only horizontal and vertical joins count; diagonal neighbours do not.
Each domino can hold only one king, so the last player picks whatever is left.
Crowns in a territory all count, so a territory can contain several.

unverified: The optional extra rules (Dynasty, Middle Kingdom, Harmony, Mighty Duel) are not covered.
